text: Those who, in the common course of the world, will call themselves your friends; or whom, according to the common notions of friendship, you may possibly think such, will never tell you of your faults, still less of your weaknesses. But, on the contrary, more desirous to make you their friend, than to prove themselves yours, they will flatter both, and, in truth, not be sorry for either.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXVII, to his son, London, July 9, Old Style 1750
